metadata.title: PISA 2022 Results Volume III: Creative Minds, Creative Schools Factsheets – Korea

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This factsheet reports PISA 2022 results for Korea using OECD’s PISA 2022 Database. The document does not specify the exact student sampling/analysis weight variable names or whether replicate weights (e.g., BRR/jackknife) were used, so the precise weighting implementation cannot be confirmed from the provided text. For PISA analyses, analysts should use the official PISA sampling weights and replicate weights supplied in the database to obtain population-representative estimates and correct standard errors under the complex survey design. The factsheet also notes that some participating countries/economies did not meet PISA sampling standards (asterisked), which affects the reliability of cross-country comparisons; this should be reflected in any downstream analysis.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This document is a descriptive OECD factsheet summarizing PISA 2022 creative thinking performance and related subgroup patterns; it does not present an empirical student-level predictive model with an explicit plausible-values (PV) estimation procedure. PVs are typically used for cognitive achievement scales in PISA, but the factsheet does not report the PV method (e.g., Rubin’s rules) or any missing-data handling strategy. Therefore, missing-data handling is not reported in the provided text, and the PV/missing-data details cannot be reconstructed from the factsheet alone.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The factsheet reports that, in Korea, 6,454 students in 186 schools completed the assessment in mathematics, reading or science (representing about 428,000 15-year-olds). The creative thinking cognitive test was implemented in 64 countries/economies in 2022, including Korea, and the factsheet presents Korea’s creative thinking results; however, the text does not describe additional analytic exclusions beyond the stated completion of the assessment.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD factsheet summarizes PISA 2022 Creative Thinking results for Korea among 15-year-old students. It reports overall creative thinking proficiency on a 60-point scale (mean score 38 in Korea vs 33 OECD average) and provides relative performance patterns compared with expectations based on mathematics and reading performance. The factsheet also describes proficiency distributions: 90% of students reach at least Level 3 (baseline), and 46% are top performers at Levels 5–6 (vs 27% OECD average). It further highlights within-Korea gaps by socio-economic status (top vs bottom quartiles differ by 6.5 points) and gender (girls outperform boys by 3.1 points). Finally, it reports associations between creative thinking and beliefs/attitudes (e.g., fixed mindset linked to lower scores) and school environment indicators (e.g., teacher valuing creativity). The document is descriptive and does not provide model-based ML performance metrics or an explicit PV/missing-data handling procedure.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This is an OECD PISA 2022 results factsheet (descriptive reporting) rather than an empirical ML/predictive study. As a result, there is no ML model training/evaluation, no target-variable prediction pipeline, and no reported PV estimation or missing-data handling method in the provided text. The extraction therefore leaves ML-related fields empty and uses the outcome summary to explain what the assessment measures and what the reported benchmarks imply for Korea.
